Mr. Keane:
Plaintiff initiates the Rule 26(f) conference with the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children
and with Ms. Hall in writing. Four items are attached.
The first two are Plaintiff's separate proposals to NCMEC and to Ms. Hall. Each states Plaintiff's
position on each subject Rule 26(f) requires the parties to discuss: the claims and defenses and the
possibility of resolution; initial disclosures; the subjects, timing, and limits of discovery; preservation;
electronically stored information; privilege, including the timing of privilege logs and an order under
Fed. R. Evid. 502(d); a protective order; and a proposed schedule. Each also states the current posture of
the case, including ECF 84.
The third is the proposal directed to Meta Platforms, Inc., so that your clients have the positions
Plaintiff has put to the other party.
The fourth is a common agenda for the matters that concern all parties, with a proposed schedule and a
method for reconciling the parties' responses. Plaintiff asks that your clients participate in those
The proposals are planning documents. They are not discovery requests, and Plaintiff does not represent
that discovery has begun. They do not waive Plaintiff's pending objections or applications.
Plaintiff requests your written response by October 30, 2026. A response applies to both clients only
where you state that both adopt it. A position stated for one client will be attributed to that client only.
Paper copies will follow by first-class mail. This email is not consent to electronic service under Fed. R.
Civ. P. 5(b)(2)(E).
Regards,
Marvelle J. Ballentine
Plaintiff, pro se
